A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendix A.4 report original ADULT experiments computing fairness-constrained equilibria across demographic partitions, cost configurations, and fairness tolerances.

after.justification: V2 retains the ADULT experiments and adds original Taiwan credit-default experiments and quantitative group-subspace diagnostics in Section 5.2 and Appendix A.5.

M1.justification: The peer-learning procedure, causal contribution model, agent best response, fairness-constrained principal objectives, and ellipsoidal restriction remain unchanged. Expanded explanations of OLS and noiseless peer observations do not introduce a different procedure.

E1.justification: V1 evaluates ADULT alone. V2 adds the Taiwan credit-default task, extending coverage from income-related decisions to credit repayment, with age, education, and marital-status partitions. The original ADULT coverage is retained.

E2.justification: The policy comparator remains the unconstrained accuracy or social-welfare optimum. No competing algorithm is added or removed from the retained experiments, and Taiwan uses the same comparator. The discussion of analytical bounds does not introduce another evaluated policy method.

E3.justification: The ADULT protocol is retained. Taiwan adds a reported evaluation of realized objective gaps against theoretical bounds and specifies random SPD matrices for both groups, extending the original scalar-multiple cost construction. Appendix A.5 also introduces quantitative projection-overlap and subspace-gap measurements.

E4.justification: Sections 5.2 and A.5 add an investigation of bound conservatism and group geometry, including subspace overlap, projector distances, and alignment with desirable directions. These address questions beyond v1's retained fairness-norm and random-cost analyses, although the new figures do not substantiate the described bound comparison consistently.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The revised analytical worst-case bounds are theoretical guarantees rather than statistical uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: V2 adds Taiwan accuracy and welfare curves across three partitions and cost models, plus numerical diagnostics such as subspace overlap of approximately 0.93 for age versus 0.80 for education and marriage. The ADULT results remain unchanged, including v1 Figures 4–5 retained as v2 Figures 6–7.

T1.justification: Table 1 replaces the general accuracy bound 4(||w*||_2 + 1) with 4 max{1, ||w*||_2}, tightens the polyhedral welfare bound from 2||w-tilde||_2 to sqrt(2)||w-tilde||_2, and restores the missing norm factor in the ellipsoidal welfare bound. Appendix A.2.1 adds an accuracy-gap lemma, a welfare tightness construction, an origin-containing-set lemma, and a bound-comparison proposition.

C1.justification: The central unified-model and convex/nonconvex fairness–optimality claims are retained. Section 1.1 adds empirical assessment of theoretical-bound tightness on Taiwan as a stated contribution beyond v1's ADULT study of heterogeneity.

C2.justification: V2 adds interpretations of bound conservatism and Taiwan performance recovery through shared predictive subspaces. It also explains the noiseless peer-learning simplification, develops practical guidance for selecting tolerances, and expands limitations to parameter-estimation errors and richer fairness requirements. These substantially extend v1's ADULT-focused interpretation and future directions.

D1.justification: Appendix A.5 adds Taiwan-specific setup details: the six-feature causal graph, rank-5 projectors, cost constructions, and desirable coordinates PAY_HISTORY, BILL_PAY, and EDU. The existing ADULT implementation description is retained; this is additional documentation for the new experiment.

R1.justification: Section 1.2 adds performative-prediction connections and acknowledges Penn and Patty's related incentive-fairness metric. Seven newly cited works include additional incentive-design research and Taiwan data/causal sources. The overall research positioning remains similar; publication and title updates concern existing works.

P1.justification: The abstract, contributions, related work, and substantial portions of the main exposition are rewritten. V2 introduces explicit research questions, moves examples ahead of general theory, consolidates Section 4, reorganizes appendix proofs, and replaces the conclusion with a broader discussion.

P2.justification: V2 redesigns Table 1 around fair-space and feasible-region columns, adds the proof-reference Table 3, introduces a tightness illustration, and adds six-panel Taiwan plots repeated in Figures 4 and 8. Existing figures are resized or relocated and captions revised; the ADULT appendix plots are retained rather than replaced.

improvement.justification: The tighter general accuracy bound, corrected welfare scaling, broader empirical coverage, and clearer organization are beneficial. However, v2's new Lemma A.4 incorrectly states a supremum of 4 throughout ||w*|| ≤ 1; at w* = 0 it is 1. Figures 4 and 8 also show welfare levels and unconstrained baselines despite claiming losses versus theoretical bounds. These problems undermine important new tightness claims, so the benefits and introduced reliability problems do not establish a clear net quality improvement.
